question: Can non-pixel metadata available alongside the photographs reproduce the discrimination without using wound pixels?
why: If recorded context alone matches the image model, apparent image-based discrimination may reflect acquisition and scheduling rather than wound appearance.
how: Fit a probe on postoperative day, acquisition features and prior submission behaviour on the same folds, and compare with the image model.

question: Does the true wound region outperform regions of identical size and shape placed elsewhere in the same photograph?
why: A single relocation can be a favourable draw. A distribution over many exactly-feasible relocations separates spatial specificity from chance placement.
how: Enumerate feasible translations exactly, draw many relocations under an overlap ceiling, and locate the true region in the resulting null.

question: Does discrimination survive stratifying on operative region?
why: Region predicts both infection risk and appearance, so pooled discrimination can be driven by case mix rather than by the wound.
how: Stratify the risk set by region, and benchmark a one-bit region indicator and CDC wound class against the image model.

question: Does discrimination survive removing infections a photograph of the incision cannot depict?
why: Organ-space infections and infections remote from the photographed incision cannot be visible, so including them inflates apparent performance.
how: Recompute discrimination excluding organ-space infections, then also excluding infections at a site other than the photographed incision.

question: Does the annotation geometry alone, with no image content, carry outcome signal?
why: If mask position and shape alone discriminate, the masking experiments inherit information from the annotation rather than from the wound.
how: Train on the binary mask as an image, and fit a probe on scalar descriptors of the mask alone.

question: Does the masking pattern replicate without task-specific fine-tuning?
why: A pattern that appears only under fine-tuning may reflect the training procedure rather than the information in the regions.
how: Repeat the masking conditions with frozen general-purpose and biomedical encoders and a linear probe.

question: Can the pipeline learn a strong image signal from this dataset at all?
why: A null spatial result is only interpretable if the pipeline can detect a signal that is known to be present.
how: Classify early versus late postoperative stage with the same pipeline and folds.
